title: An issue or PR's own timeline comment claims an issue fixed that's still open
author: kwaku-ananse
description: Compares every ordinary issue/PR timeline comment's own body against the repository's own issue set: someone writes a real GitHub closing-keyword claim ('fixes #N', 'closes #N', 'resolves #N') into an issue or pull request's own conversation thread, but GitHub never auto-closes off a comment's own text and issue #N stays open. The seventh source the claims-X family had never grown -- issue-comment-dangling-reference (the fifty-third real recipe) proved the ordinary timeline thread is a genuinely distinct GitHub object worth watching, but only ever checked whether its own #N reference existed, not whether a closing-keyword claim on it actually held.
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the comment's own updated_at, the identical shape issue-comment-dangling-reference, review-comment-claims-unfixed-issue, and issue-body-dangling-reference already established -- 0.55 within 24h since last update, 0.85 past it. Deliberately NOT flat, matching the editable-text-surface siblings rather than the permanent-text siblings: an ordinary timeline comment, like a review comment or an issue/PR body, is a text surface its author can edit at any time, so a fresh closing-keyword claim earns a grace period before being scored as a confirmed gap. A claimed issue that doesn't exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0 and named, not hidden -- that broken reference is issue-body-dangling-reference's/issue-comment-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's. A claimed issue that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A comment with no body at all is excluded outright -- there is no claim to have broken. Deliberately checks only the issue list, never the PR list -- a closing-keyword claim naming a real pull request is a future issue-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's own remit, not this one's. Fixture-only (source: "fixture") per SCOPES.md's own WIP note on issue-comment-dangling-reference: no read-only 'list issue/PR comments' tool is exposed anywhere on the-hand gateway today -- the detection logic is real, the live read waits on the Hand's gateway, and only the fixture loader swaps for a real call the day one appears.
